title: Maple Cranberry Balsamic Pan Sauce
description: Cranberries burst into a jewel-red, lightly tart glaze for roast turkey.

steps.title: Start the sauce
steps.text: Warm {oil} in the 10-inch HexClad skillet over medium-low heat.

steps.title: Build the flavor
steps.text: Finely dice any whole produce. Cook {cran} for 5–7 minutes, stirring until soft; let the berries burst.

steps.title: Simmer the base
steps.text: Whisk in {broth}, {applejuice}, {maple}, {balsamic}, {salt} gradually. Simmer gently for 5–7 minutes until the flavors come together.

steps.title: Smooth the base
steps.text: Cool just off the boil. Tilt the pan and blend with a submerged immersion blender until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Pour the slurry into the simmering sauce while whisking. Bubble gently for 1 minute until it coats a spoon.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Fold in {butter} off heat. Measure into a heatproof jug; add hot water to reach 1 cup, or simmer excess away before serving.

notes: Yield: 1 cup. Low-sodium option for the full batch: reduce fine table salt to 0.2 g and keep the same final yield. Use unsalted broth throughout. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, omit citrus or vinegar and replace its weight with water. Make ahead: chill in small jars for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes, freeze in quarter-cup portions up to 2 months. Fridge reheat: whisk over low heat to 165°F. Freezer reheat: thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat as above. Dairy swap: use avocado oil for butter, unsweetened oat milk for milk, and plain dairy-free cream cheese where needed. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 51 kcal, 0.3 g protein, 8.0 g total carbohydrate, 2.0 g fat, 0.6 g fiber, 85 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 51 kcal, 0.3 g protein, 8.0 g total carbohydrate, 2.0 g fat, 0.6 g fiber, 26 mg sodium.
